UK Creative Worker visa (Temporary Work): Overview

establishes.fact: Actors working in the UK need the Temporary Work - Creative Worker visa, unless the concession applies.
establishes.quote: A creative worker is someone who works in the creative industries, for example an actor, dancer, musician or film crew member.

establishes.fact: A certificate of sponsorship from a licensed sponsor comes first.
establishes.quote: You need to have a certificate of sponsorship from a licensed sponsor before you can apply to come to the UK to work.

establishes.fact: Applied for up to 3 months ahead; a decision usually within 3 weeks from outside the UK.
establishes.quote: 3 weeks, if you’re outside the UK

establishes.fact: The application fee is £340.
establishes.quote: The application fee for each person applying is £340.

establishes.fact: The healthcare surcharge is usually £1,035 a year.
establishes.quote: pay the healthcare surcharge , which is usually £1,035 per year

establishes.fact: A stay of up to 12 months, or the certificate’s period plus 28 days, whichever is shorter; it starts no more than 14 days before the certificate’s start date.
establishes.quote: You can come to the UK for a maximum of up to 12 months, or the time given in your certificate of sponsorship plus up to 28 days, whichever is shorter.

establishes.fact: Work of 3 months or less may use the concession instead.
establishes.quote: If you intend to work in the UK for 3 months or less, you may be able to use the Creative Worker visa concession instead of applying for the visa.

establishes.fact: A creative worker works for the sponsor in the job the certificate describes.
establishes.quote: work for your sponsor in the job described in your certificate of sponsorship
